text:
Alex Rivera: midday handoff — quick summary for the team. primary=Maria, secondary=Samir. I'm dropping notes for the next 8h shift.

Alex Rivera: What happened: we saw a burst of eviction-related 429s on the kv-cache pool between 10:12–10:35 UTC. ~12 customers hit transient tail latency spikes and some streaming connections were reset.

IncidentBot: [ALERT] 429 spike detected on cluster kv-pool-4 (10:12 UTC). Pager routed to oncall-sre.

Maria Chen: tl;dr: root cause = cache eviction storm due to a bad rollout (tokenizer v2 prewarm disabled) + a trailing fanout from a large customer warmup job.

Samir Patel: actions taken so far: rolled back tokenizer v2 flag at 10:20, increased pool size by +2 nodes (kv-pool-4 -> kv-pool-6) at 10:25, and enabled short-term prefix caching for high-QPS routes.

Lee Nguyen: customer impact: 2 customers saw degraded streaming (partial chunks), 10 customers saw increased latency >= 200ms for 30–90s. No data loss, no auth or billing issues reported.

Maria Chen: current status: steady since 10:40. Error rate back to baseline. System metrics: cache eviction rate dropped ~92%, queue depth normalized.

Alex Rivera: open gaps: automated canary check didn't catch the tokenizer prewarm toggle. need a check for prewarm flag and an alert threshold for eviction rate > 100/s.

Samir Patel: mitigations we left in place: autoscaler bump, manual routing policy to direct non-critical traffic to secondary region (eu-west fallback), temporary rate-limit for heavy warmup endpoints (limit=20r/s per token).

Maria Chen: runbooks referenced: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kv-evictions (see play 2a for rollback), https://redwood.internal/runbooks/canary-flags (add prewarm assertion).

Alex Rivera: handoff checklist for Maria -> Samir (primary->secondary):
- Primary: Maria Chen (monitor alerts + on-call Slack)
- Secondary: Samir Patel (pager backup + infra ops)
- Escalation: Lee Nguyen (eng-sre lead)
- Runbook links above + incident play ID: INC-2068-evict

Maria Chen: live monitoring instructions: watch eviction_rate, queue_depth, streaming_reset_count. Query snippets: ```
# prometheus
max_over_time(eviction_rate[5m]) > 100
sum(rate(streaming_reset_total[1m])) by (route)
```

Samir Patel: temp commands I ran: ```
# scale pool
infractl pool scale kv-pool-4 --replicas 6 --reason "eviction mitigation"
# route change
infractl routing set-policy streaming --fallback eu-west --percent 20
```

IncidentBot: [RESOLVED] Alert kv-pool-4 429 spike resolved at 10:43 UTC.

Lee Nguyen: follow-ups for postmortem: 1) add canary check for tokenizer prewarm, 2) add an automated rollback on eviction spike threshold, 3) add a customer notification template for short latency spikes.

Alex Rivera: outstanding tasks (assigned):
- Maria: create canary check PR and add to CI (ETA 24h).
- Samir: write autoscaler runbook tweak to prefer gradual scale vs sudden +2 (ETA 48h).
- Lee: draft postmortem skeleton and customer impact summary (ETA COB tomorrow).

Maria Chen: FYI I'll keep the primary watch for first 2h of the shift and hand off at 12:30 UTC if steady.

Samir Patel: I'll run the post-scale validation at 11:00 and confirm eviction rates/latency.

Alex Rivera: final notes: no ongoing customer tickets required right now. if any page hits again, escalate immediately and run the rollback playbook (see runbook play 2a). Thanks :thumbsup:

Lee Nguyen: ack. I'll schedule the postmortem meeting for tomorrow 15:00 UTC and invite SRE, Runtime, and Product.

Maria Chen: thanks all. handing off to Samir in 20m.

Samir Patel: taking primary at 12:30 UTC if no pages before then.

IncidentBot: [NOTE] On-call rotation updated: primary=Samir Patel, secondary=Lee Nguyen at 12:30 UTC.

Alex Rivera: closing thread, adding follow-ups to INC-2068 in Jira.

Samir Patel: leaving a short log snippet here for debugging: ```
2026-03-14T10:19:23Z WARN eviction: prewarm disabled, qdepth=1245
2026-03-14T10:21:02Z INFO scale: pool kv-pool-4 -> replicas=6
```

Lee Nguyen: +1 on the follow-ups. If anyone wants to pair on the canary check later ping me.

Maria Chen: ping @Oncall-Manager for capacity billing note — autoscaler bump is temporary, will revert when stable.

Oncall-Manager: noted — will flag as temporary scale in billing dashboard and set reminder for revert check in 48h.

Alex Rivera: thanks team. end of handoff.
